newsitem.title: USA: U.S. investment bankers warn of IPO pitfalls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investment bankers warn of IPO pitfalls.

text.p: The market for initial offerings has recovered from its July beating, but investment bankers and venture capitalists warned private high-technology companies Tuesday that they should still think twice before going public.

"An IPO will help a company but it's not going to make a company," said Bill Burgess, a managing director with Alex Brown. "It really is a two-edged sword and it's something I think companies have to be aware of," he said at a Red Herring magazine conference on financing.
"I would describe this bubble burst as a digestive burb," said Ken Mabbs, director of corporate finance at First Albany. "I think the idea of doing a concept deal is still quite well respected."
Filings for IPOs are back near April's record levels and venture capitalists and mutual funds are flush with cash, Mabbs said.
However, the market's view of investment risks and the conditions for IPOs have become more stringent, Maroni said.
Venture capitalists also spend more time researching management and are aware of the company's business plans, whereas some equity investors may not even read prospectuses, he said.
"I think that more value is destroyed by chasing perceived market windows than is created," Burgess said.
Missed earnings targets that cause stock prices to plunge can hurt employee morale, which can be critical at a small company, Mabbs said.
Rothrock advised companies to set earnings targets and other goals they are 90 percent sure they can achieve.
Technology stocks endured their worst beating in years in July, sending recently listed stocks into a tailspin and interrupting a record year for IPOs.
Kevin Maroni, general partner of Spectrum Equity Investors, said Internet stocks could be in for "some real corrections" when some of the companies begin missing their earnings targets.
Still, panelists said the IPO markets have rebounded somewhat, though there is more skepticism than earlier in the year.
